journal_name: International Journal of Computational Intelligence and Applications

abstracts.abstract: This paper proposes a novel neuro-fuzzy architecture termed Adaptive Cognitive Integration Network (ACIN), which fundamentally redefines the interaction between neural networks and fuzzy systems through a bi-directional reasoning mechanism. Unlike conventional neuro-fuzzy approaches that treat fuzzy inference as a preprocessing or postprocessing step, ACIN establishes a unified representation space where neural activations and fuzzy membership functions mutually inform each other in real-time. We formalize this paradigm through a set of provably convergent learning equations that simultaneously optimize synaptic weights and fuzzy rule parameters. Theoretical analysis proves that ACIN achieves exponential convergence rates under mild conditions, significantly outperforming existing sequential integration methods. The framework introduces the concept of cognitive entanglement, wherein neural feature representations and linguistic fuzzy rules co-evolve to achieve optimal pattern recognition accuracy. We further demonstrate that the proposed architecture naturally supports incremental learning without catastrophic forgetting, addressing a critical limitation in traditional intelligent systems. Experimental validation on benchmark datasets confirms the theoretical findings, with ACIN achieving 94.7% classification accuracy on complex recognition tasks. This work establishes a new theoretical foundation for hybrid intelligence systems and opens promising research directions in cognitive computational intelligence.

This paper presents a theoretically grounded improvement to the particle swarm optimization algorithm by introducing a dynamic inertia weight adjustment mechanism based on convergence state estimation. While traditional PSO variants employ static or linearly decreasing inertia weights, the proposed Adaptive Convergence-State PSO (ACS-PSO) dynamically modulates the exploration-exploitation tradeoff by monitoring swarm diversity metrics in real-time. We derive theoretical conditions under which ACS-PSO guarantees convergence to global optima for unimodal functions and demonstrate enhanced escape capabilities from local minima in multimodal landscapes. The analysis establishes relationships between swarm velocity distributions, diversity measures, and convergence rates, providing insights into optimal parameter selection. A rigorous proof demonstrates that ACS-PSO maintains the convergence properties of standard PSO while achieving faster convergence speeds and reduced computational overhead compared to adaptive variants requiring multiple parameter tuning. Extensive benchmark testing across 23 standard functions validates the theoretical predictions, showing average improvements of 23% in solution quality and 31% reduction in convergence time. The proposed framework offers a principled approach to PSO parameter adaptation that can be readily extended to other swarm intelligence algorithms.

We present a novel distributed cognitive decision support system architecture designed for real-time complex event processing in industrial IoT environments. The system introduces a three-tier cognitive architecture comprising perception, reasoning, and adaptation layers that collectively enable autonomous decision-making under uncertainty. The perception layer employs a hybrid neural-fuzzy clustering mechanism that processes high-dimensional sensor data streams with inherent uncertainty, while the reasoning layer implements a fuzzy rule-based expert system augmented with neural network-based context awareness. Crucially, the adaptation layer utilizes evolutionary computation techniques to continuously evolve decision policies based on environmental feedback. The system architecture incorporates a novel knowledge propagation protocol that enables distributed agents to share learned decision strategies while preserving individual learning autonomy. We describe the complete implementation framework, including communication protocols, data fusion algorithms, and policy optimization modules. Performance evaluation conducted on industrial manufacturing scenarios demonstrates that the proposed system achieves 89% decision accuracy with average response times under 50 milliseconds. The architecture successfully balances computational efficiency with decision quality, making it suitable for time-critical industrial applications. This work contributes a practical blueprint for implementing next-generation intelligent systems that seamlessly integrate machine learning with expert knowledge.

This paper presents an enhanced pattern recognition system architecture that substantially improves classification performance through a novel ensemble framework integrating deep convolutional features with interpretable fuzzy classification rules. The proposed system addresses the well-known accuracy-interpretability tradeoff in pattern recognition by designing a two-stage pipeline where a pre-trained deep network extracts robust feature representations, subsequently processed by a rule-based fuzzy classifier that provides human-interpretable decision boundaries. We introduce a novel feature weighting mechanism based on swarm intelligence optimization that identifies the most discriminative features for each fuzzy rule, significantly enhancing classification accuracy compared to standard fuzzy classifiers. The system incorporates a dynamic rule refinement module that continuously updates fuzzy rules based on classification performance feedback. Implementation details cover the complete pipeline from data preprocessing through final classification, including optimization strategies for real-time inference. Evaluation on standard pattern recognition benchmarks demonstrates that the proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art accuracy of 96.3% on MNIST variations and 91.8% on complex medical imaging datasets, while maintaining interpretable decision outputs. Compared to existing deep learning approaches, the system provides explicit fuzzy rules explaining each classification decision, facilitating deployment in domains requiring decision transparency such as medical diagnosis and industrial quality control.
